questions.q: Which newspaper was the only one to give Fogg's plan some support at first?
choices: The Times
The Daily Telegraph
The Morning Post
The Standard
questions.evidence: the Daily Telegraph alone hesitatingly supported him

questions.q: What made Fogg's cause more popular for a while?
choices: A letter he sent home from Paris
His portrait in the Illustrated London News
A speech made at the Royal Geographical Society
News that he had already reached Suez
questions.evidence: the Illustrated London News came out with his portrait

questions.q: What did the long article by the Royal Geographical Society argue?
choices: The trip was easy with the new Indian railway
Fogg should have gone by way of America first
A single missed steamer would ruin the whole attempt
Fogg was surely the bank robber traveling in disguise
questions.evidence: a single delay would suffice to fatally break the chain of communication

questions.q: The narrator says Fogg was set down in the betting books "as if he were a race-horse." What does this show?
choices: People bet on him the way they bet on horse races
People thought he could run faster than other men
Fogg had once owned a famous race-horse himself
Fogg planned to travel part of the way on horseback
questions.evidence: who was set down in the betting books as if he were a race-horse

questions.q: After the article, the demand for "Phileas Fogg bonds" began to "subside." What does subside mean here?
choices: Grow quickly
Become less
Stay the same
Change sides

questions.q: Why did Lord Albemarle bet five thousand pounds on Fogg?
choices: He was Fogg's oldest friend from the Reform Club
He was sure the Geographical Society was mistaken
He felt the first man to do it ought to be an Englishman
He owed Fogg a large sum of money from a past game of whist
questions.evidence: If the thing is feasible, the first to do it ought to be an Englishman.

questions.q: What did the telegram from Fix, the detective, ask the police to do?
choices: Send a warrant of arrest for Fogg to Bombay
Stop Fogg's train before it left Paris
Pay him the reward for catching the thief
Search Fogg's house in Saville Row at once
questions.evidence: Send with out delay warrant of arrest to Bombay

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: How Fogg and Passepartout crossed from Dover to Calais
How England turned against Fogg until he was called a thief
How the Bank of England caught the real robber at Suez
How Fogg's friends at the Reform Club tried to cancel the bet
questions.evidence: The polished gentleman disappeared to give place to the bank robber.
